functional_semantics.triton: Stage-2 split-KV combine only: per (b,h), nb = ceil(b_seqlen[b]/BLOCK_SEQ) (impl_triton.py L32-34); out = sum_{s<nb} exp(lse_s - m) * mid_o_s / sum_{s<nb} exp(lse_s - m) with no epsilon (L42-54).
functional_semantics.cutile: Same: real_num_blocks = ceil(seq_len/BLOCK_SEQ) (impl_cutile.py L31-33); invalid splits neutralised (L49-50); acc/sum_exp with no epsilon (L66).
functional_semantics.note: Both match impl_torch.py L13-45 except that the reference adds 1e-10 to the denominator (L45); since the denominator is >= 1 whenever at least one split is valid (the running max contributes exp(0) = 1) the difference is far below fp32 tolerance, and every benchmark row has b_seqlen = seq_len >= 1 (tensors.py L255). Stage 1 (attention over K/V) is NOT part of the operator.

stages.triton: One kernel, one program per (b,h) (L87): read b_seqlen (L32), loop over s < block_n_size with a RUNTIME, data-dependent trip count (L42), per step one head_dim vector load + one lse scalar (L43-44), online update (L45-52), store acc/sum_exp (L54).
stages.cutile: One kernel, one program per (b,h) (L86): read b_seqlen (L31), loop k in range(TOTAL_BLOCKS) with a COMPILE-TIME trip count equal to num_blocks (L41), invalid splits replaced by (-inf, 0) via ct.where (L43-50), same online update (L52-63), store acc/sum_exp into a 4-D view of the output (L66-68, L85).
stages.note: Same single-launch structure and the same per-split recurrence; skipping invalid splits by the loop bound versus visiting all splits with neutralised weights is a mapping choice (identical results; all splits are valid in the benchmark).

dependencies.triton: Sequential dependency through (max_logic, sum_exp, acc) along the split loop (L45-52); no cross-program dependency.
dependencies.cutile: Sequential dependency through (max_logic, sum_exp, acc) along the split loop (L52-63); no cross-program dependency.

reduction_scan_sort.triton: Online running-max recurrence over splits in increasing index order: old_scale = exp(max_old - max_new), acc = acc*old_scale + exp(lse - max_new)*v, sum_exp likewise (L45-52); final division once (L54).
reduction_scan_sort.cutile: Same recurrence in increasing split order (L52-63); final division once (L66).
reduction_scan_sort.note: Both are single-pass online combines (the reference is two-pass: global max then weighted sum); fp32 rounding differs only by summation order. The head_dim axis is element-wise.

precision.triton: fp32 accumulator tile (L38), fp32 scalars, natural tl.exp (L47, L49); output in mid_o.dtype via implicit cast at the store (L54, L81); no epsilon.
precision.cutile: fp32 acc/max/sum tiles (L36-39), natural ct.exp (L54-55); stored into an output of mid_o.dtype (L68, L82); no epsilon.
precision.note: Same fp32 path, same natural-base exponent, both omit the reference's 1e-10.

preprocessing.triton: block_seq_tensor.item() on a CPU scalar tensor (L72-75); output allocation (L81); BLOCK_DMODEL = next_power_of_2(head_dim) (L84).
preprocessing.cutile: block_seq_tensor.item() (L76-79); output allocation (L82); metadata-only 4-D view of the output (L85).
preprocessing.note: No data preprocessing, casts or cached state on either side; the .item() is on a CPU tensor (no device sync), as in impl_torch.py L6-7.

mutation.triton: No input written (mid_o_lse read directly, no clone); fresh output per call (L81).
mutation.cutile: No input written; fresh output per call (L82).

fq_boundary.note: The timed run() is a host .item() on a CPU scalar, one allocation and one launch on both sides; there is no preprocessing, scratch or prepacked input. bytes_expr counts one read of mid_o only; the reads of mid_o_lse (1/head_dim of mid_o), b_seqlen and the output write (1/num_blocks of mid_o) are omitted, which is a small undercount rather than a boundary mismatch. seq_len // block_seq equals num_blocks for every config case.

review_items: (non-blocking) Both implementations omit the reference's 1e-10 denominator epsilon; results agree within fp32 tolerance for every benchmark input (b_seqlen >= 1 so the denominator is >= 1), but a batch row with b_seqlen <= 0 would give 0/0 = NaN instead of the reference's 0: confirm that rows with zero valid splits are out of scope (the contract currently leaves them unspecified).
